theme: Kentucky finance; taxation; courts; land; western commodity corridor
evidence_role: Institutional discovery portal for locating early Kentucky treasury, auditor, tax, court, land, and river-related records needed for the western state layer
notes: The portal does not establish which 1792–1803 fiscal or commodity series survive. Submit a bounded research query and create series-level records before treating Kentucky as covered.

title: TOFLIT18: Transformations of the French Economy through the Lens of International Trade, 1716–1821
creator: TOFLIT18 research team
institution: Sciences Po médialab and collaborating institutions
theme: French trade; commodities; partners; ports; Atlantic markets; war
evidence_role: Product- and partner-level external benchmark for French trade and the changing market environment surrounding American Atlantic commerce
notes: A derived database compiled from heterogeneous historical trade statistics. Preserve dataset version, source publication, product classification, valuation basis, partner definition, unit, missingness, and wartime discontinuities.

title: RICardo historical trade database
date: 1787–1938; coverage is sparse and heterogeneous in early years
creator: Béatrice Dedinger; Paul Girard; Sciences Po médialab contributors
theme: bilateral trade; world trade network; partners; historical statistics
evidence_role: Global bilateral-trade context beginning near the project period and a route to underlying national statistical publications
notes: Do not assume complete annual or commodity coverage for 1789–1803. RICardo is strongest as provenance-aware context and a source-discovery tool; inspect reporter, partner, flow, valuation, currency, and source fields.

title: Sound Toll Registers Online
creator: Danish customs authorities; University of Groningen; Tresoar; project contributors
theme: Baltic trade; grain; naval stores; coffee; shipping; routes; tolls
evidence_role: Voyage- and cargo-level external benchmark for Baltic shipping and commodity movements affecting European supply conditions
notes: The registers observe passage through the Danish Sound, not total European or Atlantic trade. Port attribution, destination recording, cargo terminology, quantities, toll rules, and route selection require validation.

title: Navigocorpus
creator: Jean-Pierre Dedieu; Silvia Marzagalli; Pierrick Pourchasse; Werner Scheltjens and contributors
theme: shipping; vessels; voyages; ports; cargo; maritime risk
evidence_role: External voyage and shipping context for testing routes, vessel identities, port calls, cargo descriptions, and wartime disruptions
notes: Navigocorpus aggregates heterogeneous sources and is not a complete traffic census. Preserve the underlying source, observation type, voyage-point logic, place normalization, and uncertainty.

title: Allen–Unger Global Commodity Prices Database
date: medieval period–1914; commodity and place coverage varies
creator: Robert C. Allen; Richard W. Unger and contributors
theme: commodity prices; grain; European markets; price comparison; market integration
evidence_role: External price-series benchmark for distinguishing American institutional effects from broader commodity-price and harvest movements
notes: Published historical series contain heterogeneous qualities, units, currencies, market conventions, and interpolation. Use original source notes and construct explicit conversion and comparability rules.

title: Lloyd's Register of Ships Online
creator: Lloyd's Register and predecessor publishers
institution: Lloyd's Register Foundation Heritage and Education Centre
theme: vessels; classification; ownership; construction; maritime insurance context
evidence_role: Ship-level discovery and validation source for vessel identity, characteristics, classification, and changes in the Atlantic carrying fleet
notes: Registration and classification are not voyage or cargo observations. Coverage and field definitions changed; match ships cautiously using name, master, ownership, build, tonnage, and year.

title: Prize Papers of the High Court of Admiralty
date: approximately 1600–1860; major project relevance from captures during 1793–1803
creator: High Court of Admiralty and predecessor courts; captured merchants and crews
institution: The National Archives, United Kingdom; Prize Papers Project
repository_identifier: High Court of Admiralty HCA Prize Papers
theme: wartime seizure; neutral trade; cargo; bills; merchant correspondence; insurance; adjudication
evidence_role: Primary archival route for cargo papers, accounts, correspondence, and adjudication created by captures during the French Revolutionary Wars
notes: Capture creates severe selection bias: these records overrepresent disputed, seized, and litigated voyages. Use case, ship, capture, court, exhibit, and image identifiers and compare with noncaptured traffic.

title: Global Price and Income History Group database
date: medieval period onward; series-specific dates and places vary
creator: Global Price and Income History Group contributors
institution: University of California, Davis and collaborating researchers
source_type: scholarly historical prices, wages, incomes, and consumer-bundle portal
theme: prices; wages; income; consumer bundles; living standards; American incomes
evidence_role: Primary discovery portal for historical price, wage, income, exchange-rate, and consumer-bundle series used to construct purchasing-power comparisons
notes: Coverage, quality, population, occupation, unit, and frequency vary by series. Use the underlying source and documentation; do not combine city wage quotations and commodity prices into a national welfare index without representative weights.

title: Probing the Past: Virginia and Maryland Probate Inventories, 1740–1810
creator: Gunston Hall Plantation project; Roy Rosenzweig Center for History and New Media contributors
institution: George Mason University; Gunston Hall and contributing archives
theme: household goods; material culture; consumption; Chesapeake; slavery; wealth
evidence_role: Household-level evidence on possession, valuation, room use, material culture, and market-linked goods in Maryland and Virginia around the project period
notes: The 325 inventories represent about five percent of the underlying county inventories and mostly wealthy estates; selection criteria favored detailed or genteel households. Death inventories measure stocks at probate, not representative purchases, consumption flows, welfare, or intra-household access.

title: Annual Consumer Price Index for the United States, 1774–present
creator: Lawrence H. Officer; Samuel H. Williamson
theme: consumer prices; inflation; purchasing power; household welfare
evidence_role: Secondary long-run benchmark for sensitivity analysis of changes in the estimated cost of a consumer bundle during 1789–1803
notes: The official U.S. CPI begins much later. Early values are reconstructions with sparse price and expenditure weights. Do not treat the series as observed national inflation or as representative of rural, enslaved, Indigenous, or low-income households.

title: The Origins and Expansion of the Male Breadwinner Family: The Case of Nineteenth-Century Britain
creator: Sara Horrell; Jane Humphries
source_type: peer-reviewed research article and household-budget analysis
theme: household budgets; family income; women; children; self-provisioning; Britain
evidence_role: Comparative evidence and methodological model for measuring household composition, cash and in-kind income, expenditures, self-provisioning, and contributions by women and children
notes: British households are not proxies for American households. Use the study to design variables and interpret foreign demand; preserve its nonrepresentative occupational and regional sampling limitations.
